ledger.note: 17 December 1847: the Orange River becomes the northern boundary. Smith's proclamation 'extended the borders of the colony northwards to the Orange River'. The strip is the northern part of the Cape in Cliopatria's 1848 shape beyond the 1820 Cape. The page does not say which of the Griqua and Boer lands it covered.

region.text: Transorangia between the Orange and Vaal rivers

ledger.note: 3 February 1848: Smith proclaims the Orange River Sovereignty. 'Sir Harry Smith proclaimed British sovereignty over Transorangia on 3 February 1848': the country 'between the Orange and Vaal rivers'. A British colony in its own right (capital Bloemfontein) governed by the Cape's Governor; Cliopatria draws it in the Cape row and so does this dossier. Land of Boer settlers, Griqua and the Basotho reserve (Warden line 1849), no state: nobody.

region.text: Transorangia between the Orange and Vaal rivers

ledger.note: 23 February 1854: Britain gives up the Orange River Sovereignty. A royal proclamation of 30 January 1854 'abandoning and renouncing all dominion'; the Orange River Convention was signed at Bloemfontein on 23 February 1854 recognising independence: 'In 1854, it became the Orange Free State'. The British garrison left on 11 March 1854.

region.text: the country between the Keiskamma and the Great Kei rivers

ledger.note: 7 March 1860: British Kaffraria becomes a separate Crown colony. 'On 7 March 1860, in the wake of the great Xhosa cattle-killing, the Cape Colony again dis-annexed British Kaffraria'.

region.text: the country between the Keiskamma and the Great Kei rivers

ledger.note: 17 April 1866: British Kaffraria joins the Cape. 'It was finally re-incorporated into the Cape Colony on 17 April 1866.' The History page says 1865.

region.text: Griqualand West, the Kimberley diamond fields and Griquatown

ledger.note: 27 October 1871: Britain proclaims Griqualand West at the Kimberley diamond fields. 'on 27 October 1871 the district, together with some adjacent territory' was proclaimed British territory, 'Griqualand West Colony', after the Keate Award for Nicholas Waterboer's Griqua. A separate colony until it was 'formally united with the Cape Colony' on 18 October 1880.

region.text: Basutoland

ledger.note: 3 November 1871: Basutoland joins the Cape. Infobox 'Basutoland incorporated into the Cape Colony: 3 November 1871'; the History page: Basotho territory 'became part of the Cape Colony in 1871', after the Basotho were 'proclaimed British subjects in 1868'.

region.text: Griqualand East (Kokstad district)

ledger.note: 1877: Griqualand East is annexed. 'In 1877, the state expanded by annexing Griqualand West and Griqualand East.' (Griqualand West had been British since 1871; the Annexation Act was passed on 27 July 1877 and took effect on 18 October 1880.) The Griqua of Adam Kok III held the Kokstad country; the region name is the researcher's.

region.text: the Transvaal Republic

ledger.note: 12 April 1877: Britain annexes the Transvaal. 'On 12 April 1877, a proclamation of the annexation of the Transvaal Republic was made in Church Square, Pretoria' (Shepstone, special commissioner). Cliopatria draws the Transvaal in this row for 1877-1884 and has no South African Republic row for those years; here it is a hatched occupation, not Cape territory.

region.text: the enclave of Walvis Bay and the Penguin Islands

ledger.note: 1878: Walvis Bay joins the Cape. 'From 1878, the colony also included the enclave of Walvis Bay and the Penguin Islands.'

region.text: Griqualand West

ledger.note: 18 October 1880: Griqualand West is formally united with the Cape. 'The implementation of the act was set for 18 October 1880, when Griqualand West was formally united with the Cape Colony' (Griqualand West Annexation Act passed 27 July 1877). The land was already drawn in the Cape's tint from 1871.

region.text: the Transvaal

ledger.note: 3 August 1881: the Transvaal is handed back. 'The Pretoria Convention was signed on 3 August 1881 and ratified on 25 October'; after the Boer revolt of 16 December 1880 and Majuba (27 February 1881).

region.text: the Transvaal

ledger.note: 3 August 1881: the Transvaal under British suzerainty. 'the British agreed to complete Boer self-government in the Transvaal under British suzerainty.'

region.text: the Transvaal

ledger.note: 1884: the London Convention replaces the Pretoria Convention. certainty.note: The northern frontier (the Bushmansland mountains) and the Xhosa frontier are approximate; the Great Fish River (1780) and Keiskamma (1820) are river lines.
The Orange River (1847), the Keiskamma-Kei rivers and the colonial proclamations are sharp lines; the Namaqualand and Kalahari edge and the Transkei, annexed in stages 1877-1894, are soft.

notes:
Cliopatria's row is not the Cape alone: it folds in British possessions elsewhere. Sierra Leone (14-100 cells, later up to 347), Gambia, Gorée (Senegal) and Socotra (Yemen, from 1834) sit in the shapes from 1797; the Transvaal (1,114 cells) from 1877. All are removed in the corrections (the West African colony has its own dossier, sierra-leone-colony-and-protectorate; the Transvaal is an occupation of the South African Republic here). The row also draws the Cape in 1803-1805 when the Batavian Republic held it (dutch-cape-colony covers those years; see its merge note), starts a year late (1796; the page has 1795), and ends in 1884 although the Cape Colony lasted to 31 May 1910: this dossier carries the colony to 1910 with new keyframes from 1885, so the 'British Africa' row (1885-) must not draw the Cape again; the orchestrator should decide between ending this dossier in 1884 (delete events from 1886 and the 1885/1894/1895 keyframes) and cutting the Cape out of British Africa.

The biggest correction: Cliopatria's 1822 shape (573,477 km2) is 1.73 times the Cape Colony infobox (331,907 km2, 1822) and reaches the Orange River and lon 29.5 twenty-five years before the proclamation of 17 December 1847 ('extended the borders of the colony northwards to the Orange River'). The 1820 shape (the Cape to the Keiskamma) is used for 1822-1847. The true pre-1847 northern line (the Colesberg district, the Griqua frontier) is on no page opened; a gap-filler should open 'Colesberg' or a boundary history. Not entered for lack of dated pages: the Transkeian annexations of 1878-1894 (Fingoland, Idutywa, Gcalekaland, Thembuland, Port St Johns), the Republic of Natalia (1839-1843) and the administration of Natal from 1844 (infobox only), the Graaff-Reinet rebellions of 1799-1803. The Ninth War's Gcalekaland is Transkei land (outside the shape).

Treatment: British dependencies governed from the Cape that Cliopatria draws in this row are kept in it with their formal status in the notes: British Kaffraria (a separate Crown colony 1860-1866), the Orange River Sovereignty (1848-1854), Griqualand West (a separate colony 1871-1880) and Basutoland (1871-1884). Region names the gazetteer lacks: Transkei, British Kaffraria, Griqualand East, Xesibeland, Pondoland, British Bechuanaland ('Orange River Sovereignty' is an alias of the Orange Free State region). The Transkei page was opened and is silent. The Dutch page gives 8-18 January 1806 for the second occupation; Cape Colony's own infobox 8 January. British Kaffraria incorporation: 17 April 1866 (British Kaffraria page) or 1865 (History page). Annexation of British Kaffraria: 17 December 1847 (British Kaffraria page) or 23 December 1847 (Xhosa Wars and History pages).
